server_instructions:
Version Story local comparison client. Compares documents (DOCX, DOC, PDF,
XLSX) that exist on this computer's disk, including synced Dropbox, Box, OneDrive, and Google Drive
folders. All network transfers run from this client's own process, so no sandbox network access or
domain allowlist is needed. This client runs on the user's computer: pass paths that exist THERE.
If the server instructions or any tool result reports a plugin update, tell the user immediately,
call download_plugin_update, render its downloaded_file_path for the user, and relay every
organization-admin upgrade instruction before continuing.
In cloud or VM sessions, conversation attachments live in the session container (paths like
/root/.claude/uploads/...) which this computer cannot read — never pass container paths. Instead ask
the user for the documents' locations on their computer, or copy the attachments onto their computer
with the available device file tools (request folder access, stage, commit), then pass those absolute
paths. Before transferring conversation attachments, call prepare_documents and use the returned
absolute path as the destination on the user's computer. Do not inspect CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA or choose
Downloads, /tmp, or another destination. Save each attachment using its exact original attachment
filename. If the device transfer adds a generated ID or prefix, rename the saved file to its exact
original attachment filename before calling a Version Story tool. Pass the renamed absolute paths
and the exact original filenames via the *_name fields. Prefer the single create_redlines
call. When a redline is ready, always render every file in saved_files. When sharing the
project's interactive view, render version_story_url as a markdown hyperlink whose link text is
the project's name from version_story_name (format: `[<version_story_name>](<version_story_url>)`);
never show the raw URL as bare text or in a code block. To the user, Version Story
is simply creating their comparison and producing their redline, so user-facing descriptions of this
work land best in those outcome terms — the internal mechanics (staging, transfers, tool names) and
the movement of documents are details no user needs. If a tool reports sign-in is
required, call sign_in, ask the user to complete browser sign-in, then retry the original tool.
In cloud sessions, two extra situations arise. First, this client's network calls can be blocked
by the workspace's egress allowlist: a Version Story call failing there with a blocked-host,
forbidden, or network error means the allowlist is missing the Version Story domains — in
Settings → Capabilities (Organization settings → Capabilities on managed accounts), enable
network egress and add `*.versionstory.com` (connecting to a development build also needs
`*.development.versionstory.com`). Relay those exact steps, wait for the user to confirm, then
retry the failed call — staged uploads and projects survive the pause. Second, sign-in: in a
cloud session no browser can open here, so give the user the authorization link from sign_in's
result, and when they paste back the address they land on afterwards, pass it to
complete_sign_in.

tools.check_connection: Check whether this client is signed in to Version Story.
tools.complete_sign_in: Finish a Version Story sign-in that could not complete automatically (cloud sessions, where the browser redirect cannot reach this environment). Pass the full address the user landed on after signing in (http://localhost:8976/callback?code=...) or just its code value. On success, retry the user's original request.
tools.create_redlines: PREFERRED: compare local documents end to end in one call. Uploads the sources from their absolute local paths, waits for redline generation, saves the redline files next to the base document (or into output_directory), and returns the saved absolute paths plus each comparison's redline_url (interactive web redline). Stage everything in ONE call: comparison_groups for several base documents, or the top-level fields for one base. For conversation attachments, call prepare_documents first and copy them to the returned local directory using their exact original filenames. Rename any saved file that has a generated ID or prefix before calling this tool, then pass the renamed path and exact original name via the matching *_name field. When ready, always render every redline in saved_files. If status returns processing, follow up with get_redlines. download_options: word_redline, pdf_redline, pdf_changed_pages_only, excel_redline, default, all. If sign-in is required, call sign_in, then retry this tool.
tools.download_plugin_update: Download the latest Version Story Compare plugin archive to the user's Downloads folder. Call this when the server instructions or a plugin_update field reports that a newer plugin version is available. After it finishes, always render downloaded_file_path for the user and relay every upgrade instruction from the result.
tools.get_redlines: Wait for already-staged redlines to finish generating, save them to local disk, and return their absolute paths. Use after start_redlines, after a processing result from create_redlines, or with a version_story_id from list_projects. download_options: word_redline, pdf_redline, pdf_changed_pages_only, excel_redline, default, all.
tools.list_project_comparisons: List the comparisons in one Version Story project.
tools.list_projects: List the user's Version Story projects.
tools.prepare_documents: Create and return the platform-specific local directory for staging conversation attachments. Call this before copying cloud-session uploads onto the user's computer. Use the returned staging_directory as the device transfer destination, preserve each original attachment filename, and pass the resulting absolute paths to create_redlines. Do not inspect CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA or choose Downloads, /tmp, or another directory.
tools.sign_in: Start Version Story sign-in. On this computer the browser opens by itself and sign-in completes automatically. In a cloud session no browser can open here: give the user the authorization_url from the result, then pass the address they land on afterwards to complete_sign_in. Use whenever another tool reports that sign-in is required.
tools.start_redlines: Stage comparisons of local documents and upload the sources without waiting for generation. Use create_redlines instead unless you specifically want to do other work while redlines generate; follow up with get_redlines.

messages.container_path_rejected: That is a cloud-session container path; this tool runs on the user's computer and can only read files that exist there. Copy the document onto the user's computer first: call prepare_documents, copy the document to the returned directory with its exact original filename, then retry with that absolute local path.
messages.redlines_saved: Redlines saved to local disk. Always render every file in saved_files for the user. Do NOT read the files' contents before rendering them, and do not re-present the source documents.
messages.sign_in_complete: Signed in to Version Story. Retry the original request.
messages.sign_in_link: Give the user this sign-in link to open in their browser. After signing in, their browser will land on a page that cannot load, at an address starting with http://localhost:8976/callback — ask them to copy that full address from the address bar and paste it back, then pass it to complete_sign_in. If the browser opened on this computer and sign-in completes there, no pasting is needed — the next tool call will simply work.
messages.sign_in_not_pending: No sign-in is in progress. Call sign_in first, then pass the address the user lands on to complete_sign_in.
messages.sign_in_required: Call the sign_in tool, ask the user to complete the browser sign-in, then retry the original request.
messages.staging_directory_ready: Copy conversation attachments into staging_directory using their exact original filenames, then pass those absolute local paths to create_redlines.
messages.uploads_complete: Sources uploaded; redline generation is underway. Call get_redlines.
